info.title: OneNexus Central Auth Service — Support API
info.description: Support-team JSON RPC operations under `/support-api/*`. OAuth 2.1 / OIDC protocol endpoints under `/connect/*` are documented separately by their respective specs and the OIDC discovery document at `/.well-known/openid-configuration`.

post.summary:
Describe the first-party default S3 account and whether it has been
provisioned yet.
post.description:
Inspect the configured first-party account before provisioning. A successful response can contain no
live account yet.

200.description:
Default-account configuration plus the live account
    (or `null` if not provisioned).

post.summary:
Provision the first-party default S3 account and its account-root user.
Idempotent on the account: if it already exists the existing account is
returned and the root user is not (re)created.
post.description:
Returns the existing account on a repeat call. The root secret is returned only when its user is
first created and must be handled as a credential.

200.description:
Account provisioned (or already present). The root
    user's secret key is present only when freshly created — persist it.

409.description: A conflicting RGW resource already exists.

post.summary: List every RGW account known to the cluster.
post.description:
Use this cluster-wide inventory for Support investigations. To inspect only the configured first-
party account, use GetS3DefaultAccount.

post.summary: Finds the account that has an address.
post.description:
The first step of deleting a person's account. Support looks the account
up by the address the person gave, checks it is them, and deletes it by
the id returned here. An address can belong to a new account after the
first is deleted; an id never does, so a retried deletion cannot reach
another account. The address is personal data and is never logged.

post.summary: Deletes a person's account once none of its users is live.
post.description:
For a person who asked for their personal data to be deleted, once
support has confirmed it is them. The account goes, and with it its
address and sign-in state, so the address no longer appears in CAS's
tables; the code requests for it go with the next daily clean-up. Its
deleted users keep their ids for audit and lose the link and the
person's name. Refused while any of its users is invited, active or
suspended: remove those from their tenants first. The account is named
by the id `DescribeAccount` returned, so a repeat answers 404.

409.description:
A user of the account is still live
    (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/failed-precondition`).

post.summary:
Evaluates one principal/action/resource tuple exactly as the owning
service's PEP would, without performing the operation itself.
post.description:
Tests the supplied principal, action and resource against CAS authorization and returns the decision
and its diagnostic entities. This support operation does not execute the action being evaluated.

Creates a tenant and starts onboarding its root user. Use the returned tenant ID for subsequent
lookups. Tenant display names can repeat.

requestBody.description:
Request body. Validated by
    `[ApiController]` before this action runs.

200.description:
Tenant created. Body is a CreateTenantResponse
    snapshot of the new row.

409.description:
The idempotency key is bound to a different
    request, or the root email is already reserved
    (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/already-exists`).

post.summary: Look up a tenant by Guid PK.
post.description:
Use the ID returned by CreateTenant or ListTenants to inspect one tenant. To enumerate its members,
use ListTenantUsers.

requestBody.description: Request body. Carries the tenant's Guid PK as `tenantId`.

200.description:
Tenant found. Body is a DescribeTenantResponse
    including the live user count.

post.summary:
Page across all tenants known to CAS. Platform-admin / support
surface — there is no tenant scoping, this returns rows for every
tenant the caller is authorized to see.
post.description:
Ordering + pagination. Bidirectional cursor pagination on
the Tenant.Id UUID v7 PK. Forward (after) and
backward (before) directions both resolve to an index
range scan on the PK b-tree with no OFFSET cost. Items are
always returned in tenantId ascending order regardless of
direction — backward pages are reversed server-side. Because the
PK is UUID v7 (time-ordered), this is also a chronological listing
for free.
    Lookup and search. tenantIds returns every listed tenant
that exists, by primary key; query returns the first
limit tenants, in id order, in whose display name every
word of the text starts a word, ignoring case, accents and punctuation
(see TenantSearch). Both return one response without
cursors and keep the TenantSummary shape. The query text
is never logged.
    Authorization. CAS::ListTenants on the platform's
tenant directory. CAS resolves the caller's roles from the current
authorization store, so a token does not retain access after a role
is removed.

requestBody.description:
Request body. Use `limit` with either
    `before` or `after` for bidirectional cursor pagination, or
    send one of `tenantIds` and `query` instead to look tenants
    up by id or search them by name.

200.description:
Page of tenant snapshots. Body is a
    ListTenantsResponse; `after` is null on the last
    page and `before` is null on the first page, and both are null
    for a `tenantIds` or `query` request.

400.description:
Validation failure
    (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/invalid-argument`) — typically
    a `limit` outside 1..200, conflicting cursors, or a malformed
    `before`/`after` cursor; or `tenantIds` with
    `query`, either of them with a cursor, an empty or over-200
    `tenantIds`, or a `query` longer than 256 characters or
    shorter than 2 after trimming.

post.summary:
Page across the users belonging to a specific tenant. Platform-admin /
support surface — the target tenant is identified by Guid in the
request body, not inferred from the caller's principal.
post.description:
Ordering + pagination. Same shape as Task<IActionResult> TenantController.ListTenants(ListTenantsRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
but on the Users table, filtered to a single tenant. The
WHERE TenantId = ? AND Id > ? predicate rides the leading
column of the composite IX_Users_TenantId_NormalizedEmail
index for the tenant filter and the PK for the cursor bound.
    Tenant status is NOT a precondition. Listing the users of a
suspended or soft-deleted tenant is a legitimate operator use case
(audit, cleanup, recovery). Only a missing tenant returns 404; a
tenant that exists but is non-active still serves its user list.
    Authorization. CAS::ListTenantUsers on the platform-owned
CAS::Tenant resource for the requested tenant, for a platform
user or service client. Authorization precedes target lookup.

requestBody.description:
Request body. Same cursor + limit conventions as
    Task<IActionResult> TenantController.ListTenants(ListTenantsRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken), plus the tenant's Guid PK as `tenantId`.

200.description:
Page of user snapshots. Body is a
    ListTenantUsersResponse; `before`/`after`
    are null at the corresponding ends of the result set.

400.description:
Validation failure (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/invalid-argument`) —
    typically a malformed cursor, both cursors supplied at once, an empty
    `tenantId`, or a `limit` outside 1..200.

post.summary: Searches the users of every tenant by name or email.
post.description:
Results include users of suspended tenants and users in every lifecycle
state, deleted users included, because support investigates past
accounts too. The query text is personal data and is never logged.

requestBody.description:
Request body. Validated by
    `[ApiController]` before this action runs.

200.description: Matching users, each with its tenant's id and name.

400.description:
Validation failure, including a blank query or
    malformed cursor (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/invalid-argument`).

post.summary:
Add a roleless user to an existing active tenant. Role grants are
separate authorization-administration operations.
post.description:
Authorization. CAS::AddTenantUser on the platform-owned
CAS::Tenant resource for the target tenant. Only users may hold
this action.
    Differs from TenantUserController.CreateUser in that
the target tenant comes from the request body, not the caller's
principal. The downstream invitation logic is identical and runs
through IInvitationService.

requestBody.description:
Request body. Validated by
    `[ApiController]` before this action runs.

200.description:
User created; invitation queued. Body is
    CreateUserResponse.

409.description:
The target tenant doesn't exist or is not
    active (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/failed-precondition`), or a user with that email
    already exists in the tenant (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/already-exists`).

post.summary: Re-sends the invitation email for an existing pending user.
post.description: Authorization. `CAS::ResendInvitation` on the user's tenant. The request names only the user, so CAS reads which tenant the user belongs to first; the class policy has already limited callers to platform principals, so a missing user's 404 reveals nothing to a customer.

requestBody.description: Request body. Contains the target user id.

post.summary: Suspends a tenant, preventing normal sign-in and onboarding traffic.
post.description:
Suspends the target tenant by ID. This affects sign-in and onboarding for the tenant as a whole. Use
SuspendTenantUser to suspend a single member.

Reactivates the selected tenant. Member lifecycle state is tracked separately. Use DescribeTenant to
inspect the current tenant status.

post.summary:
Suspends an active user. Sign-in, token issuance and refresh, and
authorization checks are denied until the user is unsuspended.
post.description:
The user's role assignments are retained and become inert, because
sign-in and authorization admit only Active users; unsuspending
therefore restores the previous access in one change. CAS issues no
more tokens for the user; the person's CAS session belongs to their
account and is not ended. Access tokens already issued keep a valid
signature until they expire, and each region denies authorization once
CDC has applied the change.
    Invited and pending users cannot be suspended: accepting the invitation
would make them active again. A caller cannot suspend themselves,
because that would lock them out of the API that undoes it.

requestBody.description: Request body. Contains the target user id.

200.description: The user is suspended, or already was.

404.description:
No user with that id exists, or the user is deleted
    (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/not-found`).

409.description:
The user is neither active nor suspended, or is the
    caller (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/failed-precondition`).

post.summary:
Re-activates a suspended user with the role assignments they had
before suspension.
post.description:
The user's own state is independent of the tenant's: a user unsuspended
in a suspended tenant still cannot sign in until the tenant is
unsuspended too.

requestBody.description: Request body. Contains the target user id.

200.description: The user is active, or already was.

404.description:
No user with that id exists, or the user is deleted
    (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/not-found`).

409.description:
The user is neither suspended nor active
    (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/failed-precondition`).

post.summary: Removes a user of any tenant for good.
post.description:
The user becomes Deleted and loses its role assignments in one
transaction. Nothing undoes it: the person is invited again as a new
user. The row keeps its id for audit, and its display name until the
person's account is deleted; the account and the person's users in other
tenants are untouched. Removing an invited user revokes the invitation.
    Owners are removed too, but never the tenant's last active owner; for an
owner who must lose access now, suspend instead, which can be undone.
Removing an owner emails every owner, and the removed one, naming
OneNexus support. A caller cannot remove their own user. CAS refuses the
user's tokens from the commit, each region once CDC has applied the
change, and access tokens already issued stay valid until they expire.

requestBody.description: Request body. Contains the target user id.

204.description: The user is removed, or already was.

404.description:
No user with that id exists
    (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/not-found`).

409.description:
The user is the tenant's last active owner, is the
    caller, or changed during the call
    (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/failed-precondition`).

tenantId.description: Guid PK of the tenant the user is being added to.

email.description:
Email address. Must be a syntactically valid RFC 5322-ish address.
Uniqueness is enforced per-tenant via the
`(TenantId, NormalizedEmail)` composite index, not globally.

displayName.description: Display name shown in UIs. 1–200 chars.

attributes.description: Entity attributes keyed by their Cedar attribute name.

tags.description: Native Cedar tags keyed by tag name.

CedarDiagnosticEntity.description:
One entity supplied to Cedar for a privileged support authorization
evaluation. The list is the dynamic entity slice CAS passes to Cedar: the
evaluated principal, resource, and every relationship entity needed by the
decision. Cedar derives static action entities from its packaged schema,
so they are not repeated here.

type.description: The Cedar entity type, such as `CAS::Role`.

id.description: The entity identifier within string CedarDiagnosticEntityUid.Type.

CedarDiagnosticEntityUid.description: A Cedar entity identifier, represented as its type and ID parts.

CedarDiagnosticValue.description:
A Cedar value in the diagnostic entity graph. The `kind` discriminator
selects the concrete shape: `boolean`, `long`, `string`,
`entity`, `set`, `record`, or `extension`.

function.description: The Cedar extension function, such as `ip` or `datetime`.

value.description: The extension value's canonical Cedar text representation.

CedarDiagnosticValueCedarDiagnosticLongV.description: A Cedar signed 64-bit integer diagnostic value.

fields.description: Record fields keyed by their Cedar field name.

displayName.description:
Human-readable display name (e.g. `"Acme Corporation, Inc."`).
1–200 chars, and need not be unique. Not used for auth decisions; shown
in admin UIs only.

rootEmail.description:
Email address of the tenant's root user. Tenant creation sends this
user an activation invitation and grants the predefined
`TenantAdmin` role before activating the tenant.

rootDisplayName.description: Display name of the tenant's root user.

tenantId.description: The tenant's UUID v7 primary key.

CreateTenantResponse.description: Wire shape for a tenant returned by `CreateTenant`.

accountId.description: The id of the account to delete, as `DescribeAccount` returned it.

email.description: The account's address, as the person gave it.

displayName.description: The person's name, as first given.

liveUserCount.description:
How many of the account's users are still invited, active or suspended.
`DeleteAccount` refuses the account until this is zero.

tenantId.description: ID of the tenant to look up.

DescribeTenantResponse.description:
Wire shape for `DescribeTenant`. Identical to
CreateTenantResponse; kept as a separate type for OpenAPI
clarity (each operation documents its own response model).

context.description:
Flat JSON object of request-context facts. Values use their natural JSON
scalar representation; the packaged service catalogue supplies the
authoritative Cedar type.

cedarEntities.description:
The complete per-request entity list CAS supplied to Cedar. Compiled
policy text and policy-storage metadata are deliberately not included
in this privileged diagnostic response.

items.description: All RGW accounts known to the cluster.

limit.description:
Maximum number of items returned in the page. Defaults to
int ListTenantsRequest.DefaultLimit when omitted from the request body.
Must be between 1 and int ListTenantsRequest.MaxLimit inclusive.

after.description:
Cursor for forward pagination. When set, returns items strictly
after this cursor (i.e. with a larger Guid). Pass the
string? ListTenantsResponse.After value from the previous
response to advance one page. Omit on the first call.

before.description:
Cursor for backward pagination. When set, returns items strictly
before this cursor (i.e. with a smaller Guid). Pass the
string? ListTenantsResponse.Before value from the previous
response to move one page earlier.

tenantIds.description:
Tenant ids to look up, 1 to int ListTenantsRequest.MaxTenantIds. The response
lists each of them that exists, ordered by id; an id with no tenant is
left out rather than failing the request, and repeated ids appear
once. int ListTenantsRequest.Limit does not apply and no cursors are returned.

query.description:
Search text, at most 256 characters and at least 2 after trimming.
Every word of the query must be the start of a word in the tenant's
display name, ignoring case, accents, and punctuation, so
`an binh` finds "Công ty TNHH An Bình" and `acme` finds
"Acme-Corp". A complete tenant id finds exactly that tenant.
Returns the first int ListTenantsRequest.Limit matches in id order, with no
cursors.

items.description:
Tenant snapshots for the current page, always ordered by
Guid TenantSummary.TenantId ascending. Because the PK is
UUID v7 — a time-ordered identifier — this is the natural
creation-order listing, with no separate `created_at` index
needed.

before.description:
Cursor for the previous page. `null` when no earlier items
exist.

after.description: Cursor for the next page. `null` when no later items exist.

tenantId.description:
Guid PK of the tenant whose users to list. Obtained from a prior
`ListTenants` / `DescribeTenant` response.

limit.description:
Maximum number of items returned in the page. Defaults to
int ListTenantUsersRequest.DefaultLimit when omitted from the request body.
Must be between 1 and int ListTenantUsersRequest.MaxLimit inclusive.

query.description:
Optional search text. Only users whose display name or email matches
are returned: every word of the query must be the start of a word in
the name or email, ignoring case, accents, and punctuation, so
`nguyen an` finds "Nguyễn Văn An" and `acme` finds
`an.nguyen@acme.vn`. A complete user id finds exactly that user.
Blank means no filter. Start from the first page whenever the query
changes.

after.description:
Cursor for forward pagination. When set, returns users strictly
after this cursor (i.e. with a larger Guid). Pass the
string? ListTenantUsersResponse.After value from the previous
response to advance one page. Omit on the first call.

before.description:
Cursor for backward pagination. When set, returns users strictly
before this cursor (i.e. with a smaller Guid). Mutually exclusive
with string? ListTenantUsersRequest.After.

items.description:
User snapshots for the current page, always ordered by
Guid TenantUserSummary.UserId ascending. Because the PK is
UUID v7 (time-ordered), this is the natural invitation-order
listing.

before.description:
Cursor for the previous page. `null` when no earlier items
exist.

after.description: Cursor for the next page. `null` when no later items exist.

userId.description: The user's UUID v7 primary key.

tenantId.description: Guid primary key of the user's tenant.

PlatformUserSummary.description: User snapshot returned as a list item by `ListPlatformUsers`.

instance.description: URI that identifies this error occurrence, when supplied.

ProblemDetails.description: Error response in RFC 9457 Problem Details format.

oneOf.description:
The newly minted account-root user with its keys, or `null` when the
account already existed and the root user was not (re)created.

userId.description: Guid primary key of the user to remove, in any tenant.
Guid primary key of the pending user whose invitation should be resent.

acceptInvitationExpiresAt.description: UTC instant when the new accept-invitation link (delivered via email to the invitee) expires.

invitationSendCount.description: Total number of successful invitation sends recorded for this user.

secretAccessKey.description: Secret access key. Shown once, at creation time.

S3AccessKey.description:
An S3 access key. string? S3AccessKey.SecretAccessKey is only present on the
response that first created the key — persist it immediately.

tenant.description: Optional RGW tenant the account belongs to.

email.description: Configured default account email, if any.

rootUserId.description: Configured root user id for the default account.

oneOf.description: The live account, or `null` when it has not been provisioned yet.

S3RootUser.description: An account-root user and its freshly minted keys.

query.description:
Search text. Every word of the query must be the start of a word in
the user's display name or email, ignoring case, accents, and
punctuation, so `nguyen an` finds "Nguyễn Văn An" and
`an.nguyen@acme.vn` finds that address. A complete user id finds
exactly that user. Start from the first page whenever the query changes.

limit.description: Maximum number of items returned by this page.

after.description:
Forward cursor returned by the preceding response. Mutually exclusive
with string? SearchUsersRequest.Before.

before.description:
Backward cursor returned by the preceding response. Mutually exclusive
with string? SearchUsersRequest.After.

items.description: Matching users of every tenant and lifecycle state, ordered by user id.

before.description: Cursor for the previous page, if one exists.

after.description: Cursor for the next page, if one exists.

tenantId.description: Guid primary key of the tenant to suspend.

status.description: The current status after the operation.

userId.description: Guid primary key of the active user to suspend.

userUri.description: Canonical principal URI used by role-assignment APIs.

kind.description: Whether this is the tenant root user or an ordinary member.

Whether the user has accepted the invitation and verified their
inbox. `false` for users still in the pending-invite state.

The user's lifecycle state. Only `Active` users can sign in or
be authorized.

createdAt.description: UTC instant when the user row was created.

tenantId.description: Guid primary key of the tenant to unsuspend.

status.description: The current status after the operation.

userId.description: Guid primary key of the suspended user to re-activate.

Canonical principal URI used when assigning authorization roles to
this user.

Whether the person's account has proved its address. A new invitee's
is `false` until they join.

createdAt.description: UTC instant when the row was created.

User.description: Wire shape for a user returned by the `CreateUser` family of RPCs.

UserKind.description:
Distinguishes a tenant's owners from its ordinary members. Only the
tenant's owner page changes it.

UserLifecycleState.description:
Explicit lifecycle state of a OneNexusUser, replacing the
ad hoc "no marker at all means pending" inference that the old
`Invitation*` columns required.

instance.description: URI that identifies this error occurrence, when supplied.

errors.description: Validation messages keyed by the invalid request field.

ValidationProblemDetails.description: Validation error response. Inspect errors for field-specific messages.
